findings.current: “You’re saying pointless things in front of a Han Chinese man, Yohi.”
findings.defect: The neutral phrase “Han Chinese man” does not support Jin’s immediate complaint that Baeksang keeps calling him a “bastard,” breaking the exchange and the ensuing Bastard Family joke.
findings.rationale: Restoring the insult makes Jin’s response logically coherent and preserves the setup for Baeksang’s next line and Jin’s deadpan wordplay.
findings.replacement: “You’re saying pointless things in front of a Han Chinese bastard, Yohi.”

findings.current: “That the Pavilion Master is looking for you.”
findings.defect: Jin’s established title in this packet is “Pavilion Head,” but Namho calls him “Pavilion Master” here.
findings.rationale: Using the established title prevents terminology drift within the same chapter sequence.
findings.replacement: “That the Pavilion Head is looking for you.”
findings.source: Chapter 633, Namho preparing to return to the Fire Dragon Pavilion

findings.current: “Pavilion Master, there’s one last thing I want to say.”
findings.defect: The form of address repeats the chapter’s drift from the established title “Pavilion Head.”
findings.rationale: This keeps Namho’s address consistent with Jin’s established Murim Alliance title throughout the packet.
findings.replacement: “Pavilion Head, there’s one last thing I want to say.”
findings.source: Chapter 633, Namho’s final warning to Jin

findings.current: “Go with them. Gather the warriors under the Miao people and raise a force in case something happens.”
findings.defect: “The warriors under the Miao people” is an unnatural and unclear description of warriors belonging to the Miao tribe.
findings.rationale: The replacement is natural US English and matches the packet’s established term “Miao warriors” without changing the order’s meaning.
findings.replacement: “Go with them. Gather the Miao warriors and raise a force in case something happens.”
findings.source: Chapter 633, the Beast Miao King ordering Yayul Mok to mobilize

summary: The packet preserves its major hooks, tone, and continuity without spoilers, but contains one broken insult-based joke, two instances of title drift, and one awkward description of the Miao forces.
